question: On 30 December 2023, the EU Council issued a communication to its delegations on the admission of Bulgaria and Romania to Schengen by air and water. One part of the Annex to the Agreement is the so-called Joint Austrian, Romanian and Bulgarian statement. It contains five points outlining the continuation of joint efforts to combat ‘irregular migration’.

The Annex concludes that the measures serve as a precondition for a possible lifting of checks at the land borders between Bulgaria and Romania and those with their neighbours in Schengen. This raises a serious question as to the conditions applicable to Bulgaria and Romania’s admission to the Schengen area by air and water.

More worryingly, the conclusion to the Annex presupposes that further conditions will be imposed on the admission of Bulgaria and Romania to the Schengen area as regards land borders, and specifically the ‘improvement of the migratory situation in Austria’. I would therefore like to ask the Commission the following questions: 1.
Are we to assume that these five points really are binding preconditions for the further integration of Bulgaria and Romania into the Schengen area, including as regards land borders?
What indicator can be used to assess whether or not there has been ‘a significant improvement of the migratory situation in Austria’?
Is this ill-defined condition linked to the specific numbers of migrants returned to Bulgaria and Romania?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.5.2024) On 30 December 2023, the Council took a historic decision on the accession of Bulgaria and Romania to the Schengen area1. From 31 March 2024 Bulgaria and Romania will fully apply the Schengen acquis and checks on persons at internal air and sea borders will be lifted.

The Council agreed that a further decision should be taken for the lifting of checks on persons at the internal land borders2. The Commission will continue to provide all necessary support to the Presidency of the Council to ensure that a decision on land borders can be taken in 2024. Austria, Bulgaria and Romania presented a joint voluntary statement at the time of adoption of the Council Decision.
Discussions on the Schengen area will continue in 2024 in the Schengen Council and the Commission will support the cooperation efforts in the framework of discussions of the Schengen cycle.

In line with the Commission statement on the Council decision3, the Commission will continue to assist Bulgaria and Romania in protecting the external borders of the Union and through the stabilisation of the pilot projects, building on the successful results already achieved by it.
1 According to Article 1 of Council Decision (EU) 2024/210 of 30 December 2023 any person, irrespective of

their nationality, will as of that date be able to cross the internal air and sea borders between Romania and Bulgaria and the other Schengen Member States, and between themselves, without being subjected to border checks. https://data.consilium.europa.

eu/doc/document/ST-17132-2023-INIT/en/pdf 2 According to Recital 10 of Council Decision (EU) 2024/210 of 30 December 2023, the Bulgarian-Romanian, Romanian-Hungarian, and Bulgarian-Greek land borders are internal borders where the checks on persons have not yet been lifted. 3 Annexed to Council Communication CM 5950/23 of 30 December 2023.
